findings.title: Percent parsing extracts an arbitrary unsigned decimal fragment
findings.body: The unanchored regex does not parse the complete numeric prefix. Valid values produce incorrect results: `-25%` becomes `0.25`, `.5%` becomes `0.05`, and `1e2%` becomes `0.01`. It also accepts malformed values such as `rate25%`, while `%` throws because `match()` returns null. This can silently corrupt rates or introduce a new exception path.
findings.recommendation: Remove the trailing `%`, validate and parse the entire remaining string while preserving sign and supported numeric syntax, and handle empty or invalid prefixes without dereferencing a null match.

next_steps: Correct the percent parser and verify signed, leading-decimal, exponent, empty, and malformed percent inputs.
